{{Short description|Mathematical theory}}
In the mathematical theory of [[Kleinian group]]s, the '''Ahlfors finiteness theorem''' describes the quotient of the domain of discontinuity by a finitely generated Kleinian group. The theorem was proved by [[Lars Ahlfors]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ahlfors |first=Lars V. |date=April 1964 |title=Finitely Generated Kleinian Groups |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2373173?origin=crossref |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=86 |issue=2 |pages=413 |doi=10.2307/2373173|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=October 1884 |title=Errata |url=https://doi.org/10.2307/2369455 |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=7 |issue=1 |doi=10.2307/2369455 |issn=0002-9327|url-access=subscription }}</ref> apart from a gap that was filled by Greenberg.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Greenberg |first=L. |date=January 1967 |title=On a Theorem of Ahlfors and Conjugate Subgroups of Kleinian Groups |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2373096?origin=crossref |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=89 |issue=1 |pages=56 |doi=10.2307/2373096|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The Ahlfors finiteness theorem states that if Γ is a finitely-generated Kleinian group with region of discontinuity Ω, then Ω/Γ has a finite number of components, each of which is a compact [[Riemann surface]] with a finite number of points removed.

==Bers area inequality==

The '''Bers area inequality''' is a quantitative refinement of the Ahlfors finiteness theorem proved by Lipman Bers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bers |first=Lipman |date=December 1967 |title=Inequalities for finitely generated Kleinian groups |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02798032 |journal=[[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]] |language=en |volume=18 |issue=1 |pages=23–41 |doi=10.1007/BF02798032 |issn=0021-7670|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It states that if Γ is a non-elementary finitely-generated Kleinian group with ''N'' generators and with region of discontinuity Ω, then
:Area(Ω/Γ) ≤ {{nowrap|4π(''N'' &minus; 1)}}
with equality only for [[Schottky group]]s. (The area is given by the Poincaré metric in each component.) Moreover, if Ω<sub>1</sub> is an invariant component then
:Area(Ω/Γ) ≤ 2Area(Ω<sub>1</sub>/Γ)
with equality only for [[Fuchsian group]]s of the first kind (so in particular there can be at most two invariant components).
